GCSE and level 1 and 2 results 2026

See GCSE, level 1 and 2 results 2026 at a glance on our blog post. It explains key trends and context for this year’s results.

Our statistical release shows figures relating to 2026 results in further detail.

National Reference Test 2026

Since its introduction in 2017, NFER has been contracted by Ofqual to develop, deliver and analyse the results of the National Reference Test (NRT) in English and maths.

The NRT is administered annually and shows if student performance in English and maths at GCSE level has changed from year-to-year. This year, more than 13,000 Year 11 students took part in the NRT. You can find more detail about the NRT results in our 2026 NRT annual statement and results digest and in our blog post.

A Level and level 3 results 2026

This year, results for many A Level and level 3 qualifications were issued on 13 August 2026.

Our statistical release shows figures relating to these results.

Our blog post contains key trends and context about 2026 A Level and level 3 results at a glance.

Ofqual’s new podcast - Can I Just Qualify That?

Can I Just Qualify That?  is Ofqual’s podcast for teachers, cutting through the noise on exams, qualifications and everything in between.

Hosts Jessica Lewis-Bell and Junaid Sheikh tackle the questions that matter to people working in schools and colleges. From AI in coursework and devices in the exam hall, to results day, qualification reform, how to explain marking and grading to students and more.

You can listen on YouTube or through your chosen podcast streaming service.

Understanding grading

We have created classroom and assembly resources to help teachers, headteachers and their senior leadership teams explain GCSE and A level marking and grading to their students.

Our Understanding grading toolkit is designed to explain how qualifications are graded. It has been produced with headteachers and teachers in mind but will help anyone with an interest in finding out more. 

The toolkit answers some common questions about such topics as: 

  • how exam papers are marked 
  • how grade boundaries are set 
  • how the quality of a student’s work in their exams determines the grade they get

Proposed changes to the assessment of mathematics, physics and combined science GCSEs

Following a consultation Ofqual will continue to require exam boards to provide students with formulae and equations sheets for GCSE mathematics, physics and combined science exams for the remaining lifetime of the current specifications. It is expected that will cover exams up to 2030 or 2031.

Ofqual’s qualification reform hub

The Department for Education has announced once-in-a-generation reforms to post-16 education.

Ofqual is working with government and the education sector to deliver the most significant changes to qualifications in a generation. We are ensuring that new and reformed qualifications are high quality, well-understood and fair, so every student gains qualifications that open doors to their future.

We’ve launched a qualification reform hub, which will be the home to all the latest updates on this process of change over the next few years.

Ofqual student guide to exams and assessments in 2026

Ofqual’s student guide provides information about arrangements for qualifications and assessments in 2026. It explains what students need to know before, during and after exams and assessments.

Ofqual guide for schools and colleges 2026

This guide explains what schools, colleges and other exam or assessment centres can expect from awarding organisations regulated by Ofqual and the arrangements for qualifications in 2026. It covers qualifications typically taken in an academic year, in schools or colleges, and reported in the Department for Education’s performance tables, including GCSEs, AS and A levels, Technical Qualifications within a T Level and vocational and technical qualifications (VTQs).

VTQ information hub 2025 to 2026: key dates and deadlines

You can find information for Level 3, Level 1/2 and Level 2 vocational and technical qualifications used for progression and taken alongside or in place of A-levels and GCSEs on the VTQ information hub.

Replacement certificates

Ofqual does not hold copies of your certificates – we can’t tell you your grade or provide replacements. Certificates are held by the exam board you sat your qualification with. If you don’t know which exam board you took your qualification with, ask your school. If your school don’t know you will need to ask each exam board to do a search for you – they will charge you for this.

Contact your exam board to get a replacement certificate. If your exam board no longer exists, your certificates will have moved to an existing board. Find out who now holds your certificates.
